name: The University of Osaka
overview:
The University of Osaka, founded in 1931, is one of Japan's leading research and higher education institutions. Located in the heart of the dynamic Kansai region, it stands out for its commitment to innovation and academic excellence. With 11 faculties, 16 graduate schools, and numerous specialized research centers, the university offers a wide range of programs covering natural sciences, engineering, social sciences, and humanities.

The University of Osaka is characterized by its international and collaborative environment, welcoming students and researchers from around the world. The institution places a particular emphasis on interdisciplinary research and sustainable development, preparing its students to tackle the global challenges of the 21st century. In addition to its rigorous academic programs, the university offers opportunities for personal and professional development, creating an ecosystem conducive to innovation and leadership.

With a rich tradition of excellence and a forward-looking vision, The University of Osaka is a pillar of education and research, significantly contributing to scientific advancements and social progress.
administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application. You will apply to the Admissions Assistance Desk (ADD).
Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Photocopy of passport/residence permit (valid more than 6 months after return)

  • ID photo

  • Academic transcripts (available on intra)

  • Copy of your highest diploma (baccalauréat)

  • Statement of purpose and Research plan (that follows the template provided)

  • Proof of language proficiency (Japanese and/or English); Tepitech available on intra

  • Expected Graduation Certificate

  • Certificate of Enrollment (available on intra)

To be given to the campus administration:

  • The addendum to the contract

  • EPITECH re-registration dossier

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.

  1. Receipt of the letter of acceptance from Osaka University

Once your application has been sent, the partner university will study your application and if you are accepted, you will receive an admission letter.

3. Visa application

Once you receive your letter of acceptance, you will be able to apply for a visa.

Upon your arrival:
During your immigration check after the first landing in Japan, show QR codes on the Visit Japan Web screen to an officer and answer questions.
Your COE will be exchanged with a “Residence Card” upon your entry in Japan.

4. Health and insurances

All students at Osaka University are required to apply for an insurance plan. This will cover unforeseen disasters and accidents during educational and research activities and commuting to school. Natural disasters such as earthquakes are not included in the insurance. For further details, please ask Osaka University CO-OP.
Exchange students who will stay in Japan more than 3 months must join the National Health Insurance (NHI) regardless of the kind of insurance they may already have. This is a strict legal requirement in Japan. Once you arrive in Japan, you must complete the required procedures at your local city/ward office.

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.
To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/japon
Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.

  1. Campus life

Osaka University is organized in 4 campuses:

  • Toyonaka Campus

  • Minoh Campus

  • Suita Campus

  • Nakanoshima Campus

The Graduate School of Information Science and Technology is located on the Suita Campus. There is an inter-campus shuttle bus service that connects each campus.

Osaka University has 2 hospitals, 4 libraries (the main one is located on Toyonaka Campus), and its own museum.

You can live on campus in the different accommodation available (cf. Accommodation section).
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here and here)

The Graduate School of Information Science and Technology is located on the Suita Campus. There is an inter-campus shuttle bus service that connects each campus from another.  

Osaka University operates several dormitories. However since their capacity is limited, most of the international students need to find their housing outside of campus. We recommend you start looking for housing ASAP if you cannot reserve a room at a university dormitory. Do not wait till a peak season (mid Feb.-March and mid Aug.-Sep.) in the real estate market around the campus.

Rent goes from 12700 to 13700 yen/month (about 80€).

courses:
Credits

Students must take a total of 24 local credits, i.e., 12 credits per semester to obtain 60 ECTS for the year, not counting EIP credits.

Academic Calendar

1st (Spring) Semester: April - August (5 months)

2nd (Fall) Semester: October - Mid-February (5 months)

Department and Courses

Epitech students are enrolled in the Graduate School of Information Science and Technology (Research Lab)

  • English Presentation Skills (2 credits)

  • Introduction to Information Networking (2 credits)

  • Exercices on Computer Science I (2 credits)

  • Exercices on Computer Science II (2 credits)

  • Introduction to Intelligent System (2 credits)

  • System Interface Design (2 credits)

  • Fundamentals of Computer Science (2 credits)

  • Mobile Communication Protocols (2 credits)

  • Big Data Analytics (2 credits)

  • Japanese I (4 credits)

  • Japanese II (4 credits)

Important notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).

  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.

  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.

  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.

  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial overview (4th yeat at Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees at the partner university.
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.)


Other expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: from 800€
  • Visa: 18€
  • Additional insurance: 300-600€ depending on the coverage (same as above)
  • Textbooks


Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the Japanese yen. 1 € = 176¥ (rate in October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

The cost of living depends on the individual, but in general more than 85,000 yen is required per month (about 500€).


  • Housing

~200€ if you live in the dormitory (35 000 yen),

~300 to 500€ if you live off-campus. The price of an apartment in the city center is approximately the same as a mid-size city in France.


  • Food & eating out ~250-300€ / month

Around 6 euros for a meal in a basic restaurant

Around 15 euros for a meal in a mid-range restaurant

The price of basic food is about the same as in France (Paris), except for imported products which will be more expensive and local products which will be cheaper. In general, eating out in Japan is inexpensive compared to Europe or North America.


  • Gas, electricity, water ~40€


  • Transportation

Hirakata campus: 1340 yen = 8€ (round trip/day)


  • Phone, internet ~20-50€

We recommend you to make a mobile contract at one of discount mobile phone companies in Japan, for example: "Rakuten Mobile", "UQ mobile" provided by KDDI, "Y!mobile" by SoftBank, and Sakura Mobile. With a new SIM card, you can use your own smart phone in Japan.


  • National Health Insurance ~12€
  • Leisure ~80-150€


The prices are indicative and may vary!


Additional information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

Students can find the government-approved information site for studying in Japan operated by the Japan Student Services Organization through the link here.

A previous student has recommended Rakuten for the phone plan because it is the cheapest for a good amount of data.


Food

The price of food will vary depending on whether you wish to cook for yourself or not. Japan has a great system of readymade meals prepared at supermarkets and convenience stores that are very cheap. You can therefore pay around 8€ a day for eating your lunch and your dinner from there. You can sometimes pay even less as some supermarkets put discounts on meals after a certain hour. It is entirely possible to eat a lunch and dessert for 4€ in Japan by waiting for those discounts. It is popularly said that those meals go bad after one day and you must eat them the day they are made.

If you have a fridge, you can store them for up to two weeks. It is therefore possible to eat for 40€ a week in Japan.

Vegetables, fruits, and rice is very expensive in Japan. A kilo of rice itself costs between 4€ and 5€. Anything meat related is mostly cheap.

It would overall cost as much as to eat readymade meals or cooking for yourself depending on how you eat.
